what_this_is: The Workshop rows for sending a message from the person's AI: an email (Amazon SES or Resend), a text (Twilio) or a Messages message on the person's own Mac, to one person or a list, and turning a document into a message body first. Each provider is one row here and one entry in read-data/message-providers.json; the person's own key reaches the one process on private pipes and is never in the request. Two rows pace a sending inbox and sort what comes back (bounces, complaints, replies) by the pacing and outcome rows of read-data/inbox-pacing.json.

payload.label: Send an email with Amazon SES
payload.job: Send an email, to one person or a list, through my Amazon SES account
payload.description: Give recipients (a list of addresses; to for one), region (such as us-east-1), and the words: subject and text (drawn as an email in the look the person wears, read from their screen-look records (the shipped look until they choose one; an email whose look cannot be read is not sent), with its mark from the mail row's brand and made_with) or your own html, markdown for a written email (it also goes as a BCC to the account's own address, and answers sent_copy), or template (a template name from read-data/message-templates.json, or your own templates) with variables; kind names what it is for the account's limits (sign-in-code, message ...). Every email comes from the account's own mail row (records `mail-settings` `settings:mail`, copied from read-data/mail-settings.json the first time), never from the request; each address may be sent only so many emails of a kind (per_person), the day keeps room for sign-in codes (daily), a proof address is written down and never sent, and every email is written down under its address. Each recipient is sent to on their own and answered on their own: sent holds { recipient, messageId } or { recipient, error } with limited, unknown (it may have gone; it is not sent again) or suppressed. The held SES keys reach the one process on private pipes; they are never shown.

provenance.source: bitfield-packages broadcast-delivery (Amazon SES adapter) and resend-email-sender (templates, headers), ported

record_model._what: Moved here from tools/keep-a-record-library-valid, where they were held unchanged after the engine's one record model left it (old trillion src/record-model.json and src/record-indexes.json): the kinds this tool's job keeps, each as old trillion declared it.

payload.label: Send an email with Resend
payload.job: Send an email, to one person or a list, through my Resend account
payload.description: Give recipients (a list of addresses; to for one) and the words: subject and text (drawn as an email in the look the person wears, read from their screen-look records (the shipped look until they choose one; an email whose look cannot be read is not sent), with its mark from the mail row's brand and made_with) or your own html, markdown for a written email (it also goes as a BCC to the account's own address, and answers sent_copy), or template (a template name from read-data/message-templates.json, or your own templates) with variables; kind names what it is for the account's limits (sign-in-code, message ...). headers can carry In-Reply-To, References or List-Unsubscribe (names are limited to letters, digits and hyphens, values to one line of 4 KiB); idempotencyKey makes a retry safe. Every email comes from the account's own mail row (records `mail-settings` `settings:mail`, copied from read-data/mail-settings.json the first time; its from must be on a domain verified in Resend, see tool:list-email-sending-domains), never from the request; each address may be sent only so many emails of a kind (per_person), the day keeps room for sign-in codes (daily), a proof address is written down and never sent, and every email is written down under its address. Each recipient is sent to on their own and answered on their own: sent holds { recipient, messageId } or { recipient, error } with the provider's own status, error name and reason, and limited, unknown (it may have gone; it is not sent again) or suppressed. The held key reaches the one process on a private pipe; it is never shown.

provenance.source: bitfield-packages resend-email-sender (templates, headers, idempotency) and broadcast-delivery (Resend adapter, list sending), merged and ported

payload.label: Send a text message with Twilio
payload.job: Send a text message, to one number or a list, through my Twilio account
payload.description: Give recipients (phone numbers with country code; to for one), from (a number on the Twilio account), account_sid (the account's id) and text (or subject when there is no text). Each number is sent to on its own and answered on its own: sent holds { recipient, messageId } or { recipient, error }. The held auth token reaches the one process on a private pipe; it is never shown.

payload.label: Send a message in Messages on this Mac
payload.job: Send a message to one person or a list from the Messages app on the person's own Mac
payload.description: Give recipients (phone numbers or Apple ids Messages knows; to for one) and text. Each recipient is sent to on their own and answered on their own: sent holds { recipient } or { recipient, error }. The text goes to Messages as its own argument, never inside the script. If the Mac has not allowed this to control Messages, nothing is sent and the answer says what to allow in System Settings, Privacy and Security, Automation.

provenance.source: bitfield-packages imessage-messages-sender (the Messages script as DATA, permission classification), ported

payload.label: Turn a document into a message body (runs on your computer)
payload.job: Turn a document I wrote (headings, paragraphs, images, a quoted reply) into the HTML and plain-text body of a message, ready to send
payload.description: Takes a request file { document_nodes: [{ id, kind, props, children, visible }] or one root node, options? } and writes { body_html, body_text, inline_refs, degraded }. Text and heading kinds become paragraphs and headings with a plain-text line each; image and media blocks become inline_refs { cid, fetch_ref, mime } for the sender to attach; blocks marked as a quote become one blockquote with > lines; hidden subtrees are skipped; a block kind it does not know falls back to its text and is listed in degraded, never dropped silently. options.kind_renderers maps your own block kinds to paragraph, heading1 to heading3 or media. It names no mail provider.

request.description: Path of the request JSON file

output.description: Path to write the result JSON to

output_schema.description: Exit 0 and one summary line: the HTML and text sizes, the number of parts and of degraded blocks. The output file holds { body_html, body_text, inline_refs, degraded }.

invoke.say: This runs on the person's own computer, from the root of the Workshop checkout. Write the request file from the document, run `run`, then read the output file. Hand body_html and body_text to the sending tool as html and text. Tell the person about every entry in degraded (a block that could not be shown as itself). If you cannot run commands, give them these steps.

payload.label: Sign someone up for an email course (sends through Resend)
payload.job: Sign a person up for an email course after they agreed to it, keep their consent in my records, send the first lesson now and queue the others
payload.description: Give email, consent (true only when the person agreed in the words of course.consent_text), course (id, public_origin as an https site root, checkout_url, from, mailing_address, consent_text, consent_version and 2 to 12 lessons { delay_hours, subject, article_url, text_lines, html_lines } where every lesson carries {{unsubscribeUrl}} and {{mailingAddress}} and the first has delay_hours 0), source (where they signed up, optional) and provider (resend). Nothing is sent without consent, a sender and a mailing address. Records the consent with its words, version, time and source; queues each later lesson at its time (tool:send-due-email-lessons-with-resend sends them); sends lesson 1 with List-Unsubscribe headers; signing up again sends nothing twice. Answers { status: enrolled, already_enrolled }.

payload.label: Send the email lessons that have come due (through Resend)
payload.job: Send each email-course lesson whose time has come to the people still signed up, once each, and retry a failed one later
payload.description: Optional limit (up to 50 per run) and provider (resend). Finds the queued lessons whose time has passed, sends each to a subscriber who is still signed up and has not had it, marks it sent, and removes the queue entry. A failed send queues its own retry (up to three, each later than the last). Answers results [{ lesson_index, status: sent, already-sent, unsubscribed or failed, why? }] and said.

provenance.source: bitfield-packages myletter-newsletter (email-course deliver, run when a lesson comes due), ported

payload.label: Save someone's interest in one email update
payload.job: Keep the consent of a person who asked for one email if a course becomes available, without sending anything
payload.description: Give email, consent (true only when the person agreed in the words of course.consent_text) and course ({ id, public_origin as an https site root, consent_text, consent_version, capture_only: true }) and source (optional). Records the address with the words, version, time and source of the agreement as pending. Sends nothing, queues nothing; saving the same agreement again changes nothing. Answers { status: interest_saved, already_saved }.

course.consent_text: Email me one update if the free lesson series becomes available.

payload.label: Stop sending an email course to someone who unsubscribed
payload.job: End a person's email course subscription from the token in their unsubscribe link, so no further lesson is sent
payload.description: Give token (the unsubscribe token in the link the person was sent). Marks the subscription unsubscribed with the time; an unknown or already used token answers unsubscribed too. Answers { status: unsubscribed }.

payload.label: Who agreed to get which emails
payload.job: Show who agreed to get which email list, in what words, when and from where, and whether they still do
payload.description: Optional list (one list's id) and status (active, pending or unsubscribed). Reads every consent in my records: email courses and one-update interest lists. Returns people [{ email, list, kind: course or update, status, consented_at, consent_text, consent_version, source }], agreed (the addresses that can be sent to now, each once) and said. It changes nothing; hand agreed to a send tool as recipients.

provenance.source: bitfield-packages myletter-newsletter (the subscription and interest records its consent logic keeps), read back

payload.label: Pace sends from an inbox
payload.job: Say when each address on a list may be emailed from one sending inbox, so a new inbox warms up slowly, sends only on chosen days and hours, and stops when its mail bounces
payload.description: Give time_zone (the inbox's), recipients and a pacing row (pacing: new-inbox-warmup or saturday-local from read-data/inbox-pacing.json, or your own pacing_row): a ramp of sends a day by the inbox's day number, the least gap between sends, weekdays, local hours, how many days to leave an address after it was sent to, and when to pause (a share of hard bounces or any complaint among the last sends). Add history (every send this inbox made), outcomes (from tool:sort-bounces-and-replies) and suppressed addresses. Returns due_now (send these now, through a send tool), schedule (a slot for every address that may be sent to, in local time with its ramp day), held (each address left out and why: suppressed, bounced, unsubscribed, replied, sent to recently, listed twice, not an address, or the inbox is paused) and paused. It sends nothing and keeps nothing; every number, day and hour is a row you can change.

pacing.description: A pacing row id from read-data/inbox-pacing.json: new-inbox-warmup or saturday-local.

pacing_row.description: Your own pacing row: { id, ramp: [{ from_day, per_day }], min_gap_minutes, weekdays, hours: { from, to }, leave_address_days, pause_when: { last_sends, bounce_share_at_least, complaints_at_least } }.

time_zone.description: The sending inbox's IANA time zone; weekdays and hours are read in it.

first_send_at.description: When this inbox first sent; its local day is day 1 of the ramp. Defaults to its earliest send in history, else the first send planned now.

provenance.source: outreach methods that send from a separate, warmed-up inbox at a set pace and stop on bounces and replies, generalised into pacing and outcome rows

payload.label: Sort bounces and replies
payload.job: Sort the bounces, complaints, unsubscribes and replies that came back from emails I sent, and say which addresses never to send to again, which to retry and which people wrote back
payload.description: Give events as your provider or mailbox gave them and event_source (plain, resend-webhook, amazon-ses-notification or mailbox-message from read-data/inbox-pacing.json, or your own event_source_row naming where the recipient, type, status, subject, text and time sit). Each event is read into those fields and the first outcome row whose every condition holds (a field equals one of its values, contains one of its words, or matches its pattern) names its kind (hard-bounce, soft-bounce, complaint, unsubscribe, reply, auto-reply, delivered) and action (suppress, stop-sequence, retry-later, hand-to-person, none). Returns outcomes (hand them to tool:pace-sends-from-an-inbox), suppress, stop, retry (with when), replies and the unmatched events. It sends, deletes and keeps nothing; your own outcome_rows replace the shipped ones.

events.description: The bounces, complaints, delivery notices and replies that came back, as the provider or mailbox gave them.

event_source.description: An event-source row id from read-data/inbox-pacing.json: plain (default), resend-webhook, amazon-ses-notification or mailbox-message.

event_source_row.description: Your own event-source row: { id, fields: { recipient, type, status?, subject?, text?, at? } }, each a dot path into an event.

outcome_rows.description: Your own outcome rows in order: { id, when: [{ field, equals | matching | pattern }], kind, action, retry_after_hours?, says? }. The first whose every condition holds wins.

provenance.source: outreach methods that send from a separate, warmed-up inbox at a set pace and stop on bounces and replies, generalised into pacing and outcome rows
